evidence.title: File:Fresh cakes cooling.jpg
evidence.description:
More late night cake making, this time I'm making a coffee and Walnut cake for someone at work.  She doesn't know it yet but I know she like coffee and walnut cake, I hope she likes this one.  There's a double shot of espresso in the cake and a double shot in the icing which I'm making here.  See how the Chef whizzes.  To make this one you have to cream the butter and sugar together which would be a pain in the bum without the Chef.  Not that I'm scared of a bit of graft but it's handy sometimes.  Making buttercream icing is easy with it too.  Thanks mum.
   Coffee and Walnut Cake 
250g unsalted butter
250g caster sugar
250g plain flour (or use self raising and leave the baking powder out)
3 tsp baking powder 
1 ristretto double espresso (or 1 tsp coffee essence or instant in 1 tbsp of water)
  100g unsalted butter
200g icing sugar
1 ristretto double espresso (or 1 tsp coffee essence or instant in 1 tsp of water)
  Walnuts - enough to cover the top
  Cream the butter and sugar until is well, er, creamed.  Pale and fluffy is good apparently
  Stir in the coffee (cold) at which point mine curdled but I don't think it matters.
  Sift in the flour and baking powder and gently fold it 'til it's all combined.  Dont beat it else you'll duff in the gluten in the flour and your cakes will be flat.
  Divide it in to two 21cm base lined and  greased cake tins and pop in the oven for 25 minutes at 180C.  It should spring back if you touch it lightly.
  To make the icing beat the butter, icing sugar and coffee together until it's all combined.  Once the cakes are fully cooled spread the icing in the middle and on top and cover with walnuts.  Which I'm going to go and do right now...
 
G9 sat on the big tripod on a timer and stopped down enough for some depth of field and to get the chef whizzing round.  Cropped to my favoured 3:2 ratio and a tiny bit of unsharp mask to feed my addiction.
